title: Product Class and Service Level in Wrong-Item Refund Shares, Cartwise Grocery Orders
content:
**Cartwise Grocery Orders — product class points on the wrong-item refund.** When a wrong-item refund is figured for a line whose approved replacement was not the product handed over, the class of the product on that line and the way the order reached the customer add share points to the wrong-item keep share.

## The rule

The wrong-item class points are added to the keep share before it is applied:

- a **perishable** product on an order whose service level delivers adds **10 share points**;
- a **pantry or household** product on an order whose service level delivers adds **5 share points**;
- any other product, or any product on a pickup order, adds none.

The product class is the item category shown on the line's billed entry. A service level "delivers" when its fulfilment mode is delivery — No-Rush Delivery, Standard Delivery, Priority Delivery, Express 30 Delivery and Stock-Up Delivery. Curbside Pickup is the pickup service level.

## Decision table

| Item category on the line | Delivery service level | Curbside Pickup |
|---|---|---|
| Perishable | 10 points | none |
| Pantry | 5 points | none |
| Household | 5 points | none |
| Any other category | none | none |

## How the points work (hypothetical figures)

Share points are percentage points added to the keep share itself, not a separate percentage of the refund. With a hypothetical keep share of 50 percent, a perishable product on a Standard Delivery order carries a share of 50 plus 10, that is 60 percent, and that 60 percent is what applies to the wrong-item value. The same product on a Curbside Pickup order would carry the 50 percent unchanged.
